about: The only things the appearance training set records per building (owner, 2026-10-21): a main colour and an accent colour from fixed palettes, and a general style from a short menu. Everything else is randomised by the generators. Commercial buildings only for now; the residential rows already look right.

style.says: 1870s-1900s wood-frame shop-and-flats: ornate cornice, tall narrow windows, bay windows over a storefront
1905-1930 masonry or stucco block of 2-6 storeys: storefronts, regular punched windows, a projecting cornice, sometimes bays
exposed red/brown brick warehouse, loft or workshop: big industrial windows, plain parapet
pre-war stone or terracotta office/hotel/bank: Beaux-Arts or Art Deco, piers, carved cornice or setback crown
1945-1975 plain box: ribbon or aluminium windows, panels, flat roof, little ornament
exposed concrete: heavy piers or fins, deep-set windows, raw grey surfaces
glass curtain wall or mostly-glass high-rise
1990s-today mid-rise: mixed panels, glass and render, ground-floor retail, balconies or bays
one or two storeys of shop or strip retail: plain stucco or block wall, signage, flat roof
Chinatown commercial: painted balconies, tiled eaves or pagoda trim, red/green/gold accents
none of the above fits, or the style can't be told
